title: Residency proofpack composer and SLA-bound export pipelines
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers require not only a way to pin request residency to regions, but an auditable, time-bound artifact that proves where customer request payloads and derived telemetry lived over a given retention window. Existing exports are manual, inconsistent across tenants, and do not include recent retention policy deltas or proof of processing (signatures/timestamps).

Goal: Build a 'proofpack composer' that aggregates residency decisions, retention policy versions, routing events, and evidence artifacts (logs, signed routing assertions, storage location hashes) into a single downloadable package per tenant and per export window. Provide an SLA-aware export pipeline that can be scheduled or triggered on-demand, with verifiable signatures and an automated delivery channel (S3/secure transfer).

Success criteria:
- Package format defined and documented (manifest + signed slices).
- Proofpack contains: tenant config snapshot, policy version history, per-request routing trace for export window, retention-decision records, storage URIs with checksums, and platform-signed timestamp assertions.
- Export job completes within SLA (default 12h for standard, 4h for priority enterprise) for export sizes up to 100GB.
- RBAC and KMS-integrated signing; exports can be encrypted with customer keys.
- Console UX to schedule recurring exports and view export history + a verification endpoint for auditors.

Non-goals: Long-term bulk replays of raw request payloads (we will include pointers and checksums, not necessarily raw payload unless tenant opts in).

Approach:
1) Define canonical proofpack schema (manifest, metadata, signed attestations). Owner: Product + Compliance.
2) Implement lightweight export orchestrator (stateless job controller) that queries routing history, policy store, and storage index; composes artifacts in staging S3. Owner: ENG runtime + infra.
3) Integrate KMS/HSM signing flow and optional customer key wrapping. Owner: Security.
4) Console controls: schedule, immediate export, retention-window selector, and verification UI. Owner: Console PM/Design.
5) Metrics & monitoring: export duration, failure reasons, size distribution, latency vs SLA. Owner: Observability team.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- We will prioritize manifest completeness over including raw payloads to limit exposure and S3 egress costs.
- Signed assertions must be reproducible; we will maintain a versioned signing policy.
- For very large tenants we will support chunked exports with streaming checksums; initial rollout capped at 100GB SLA.

Stakeholders: Compliance (Asha Patel), Security (Diego Ramos), Runtime (Anika Gupta), Console (Ravi Nair), Customer Success (Elena Morales).

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (alpha): Internal teams + two SOC2 customers, manual trigger only.
- Phase 2 (beta): Scheduled exports + console controls for select customers.
- Phase 3 (GA): Open schedule + SLA tiers + customer-key encryption.

Open questions:
- Exact manifest schema fields for third-party auditors (action: Compliance to propose).
- Performance budget for indexing routing traces for customers with >1M daily requests.

Related docs and links: [PRD draft] https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RES/Proofpack+Composer, [Design mockups] https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/proofpack-ui, [Threat model] https://intranet.redwood.ai/security/proofpack-threats
